title: Token-swap race on Dedicated gateway triggers ephemeral privilege breach
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: A race during token swap in the Dedicated gateway forwarding path can briefly accept an old session token for a different org while a node is rehydrating. This leads to intermittent cross-org request acceptance for a <~2s window under load when connection multiplexing and token rotation coincide. Impact: multiple Dedicated customers reported surprising 200 responses for requests scoped to a different org. Behavior observed in both Hosted-like control plane and Private deployments using the dedicated gateway image.

Background: The gateway forwards requests to per-customer routing contexts. To reduce tail latency we keep connection pools and reuse long-lived gRPC channels; during token refresh we swap the auth token on the channel. Under heavy concurrency the channel auth header swap can race with an in-flight request that uses cached routing metadata, allowing the previously valid token to be used against the next request if connection sharing hasn't been fully drained. This is exacerbated by: connection reuse across org contexts, delayed KV cache invalidation during rotation, and a small ordering window in swapAndDispatch logic.

Why this is urgent: Customers with Dedicated capacity expect strict isolation. Several customers opened escalations citing incorrect resource access and one customer provided a reproducible trace showing a 1.2s window where requests were accepted with incorrect org-scoped tokens. We classified this as P0 because of confidentiality/authorization implications.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy the current dedicated gateway image (gateway-2.7.x) with connection multiplexing enabled and per-org channel reuse set to false
Create two orgs (OrgA, OrgB) with active tokens; set high QPS load that causes channel reuse (e.g., 200 rps across 50 clients)
Trigger concurrent token rotations for OrgA while rapidly sending interleaved requests signed for OrgB on the same worker node
Observe traces in the gateway: request A (old token) accepted and routed to OrgB backend before token cache was cleared; reproduce by correlating request ids and auth headers in access logs
mitigation: Hot patch deployed to gateway-2.7.9: add atomic swap barrier on channel auth header and drain-in-flight per-channel prior to accepting new tokens (rolled to customer-facing nodes)
Temporarily disabled cross-org channel reuse via config REDWOOD_GATEWAY_CHANNEL_SHARING=false for affected Dedicated clusters
Blocked further automatic token rotations for impacted customers until patch applied via control plane toggle
Notified SecOps and affected customers with recommended steps and temporary compensating controls
root_cause: Race condition in gateway swapAndDispatch path: token replacement was non-atomic relative to channel reuse and per-request routing metadata. The channel-level auth header update could be observed by a subsequent request before the gateway finished draining in-flight requests and invalidating routing caches for the previous context.
fix_plan: Primary fix: implement channel-level sequence numbers and require per-request auth bind validation so that a request must match the channel sequence it was created under (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3245)
Add aggressive KV-cache invalidation on rotation and a short per-channel quiesce window (default 250ms) configurable by env var
Add unit + integration tests simulating token swap under multiplexed channels and concurrency harness (tests in runtime/auth_swap_test.go)
Post-deploy: run chaos test for 48 hours on dedicated staging fleet to validate under high QPS and rotation frequency
deploy_plan: Cut release gateway-2.8.0-rc1 with auth swap fixes
Canary deploy to 3 dedicated customer clusters (low-risk sentinel customers) for 6 hours
If stable, ramp to remaining Dedicated clusters over 12 hours; for Private customers provide hotfix image and manual rollout playbook
If rollback required, revert to gateway-2.7.9-hotfix and re-enable channel_sharing config
rollout: Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% across Dedicated. Private deployments will receive an image and runbook; coordinate with Solutions Eng. Automated rollback if 5xx or authorization anomaly rate rises >0.1% in any canary cluster.
customer_escalations: Acme Analytics (dedicated-prod-east) - reported cross-org routing; timeline & traces provided; currently on hotfix image
ClearSight AI (private on-prem) - observed 403->200 progression during scheduled key rotation; provided local logs; Solutions Eng engaged
GammaRetail (dedicated-eu) - alerted on anomalous auth header mismatch; on watchlist for canary
